name: Talbros Automotive Components Ltd
title: Talbros Automotive Components Ltd - 505160 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record Q1 FY27 revenue of INR242 crore (+15% YoY) and EBITDA margin 17.6%, but supply-side evidence is thin: no capacity-discipline signal, margin pressure from steel/aluminium and wages, and forging guidance cut from ~INR400 crore to ~INR340 crore.

capex.quote: Our planned capex is about INR103 crores for the year across gaskets, forgings, heat shields and to try and meet the demands of the OEM.

triggers.label: Forging FY27 revenue cut to ~INR340 crore
triggers.quote: This year, we should close at about INR340 crores around, but 2.5%, 3% here and there.

triggers.label: Margin pressure from steel and aluminium
triggers.quote: Margins during the quarter witnessed temporary pressure on account of elevated commodity prices, particularly steel and aluminium

triggers.label: Data-centre gasket revenue ~5% of gasket
triggers.quote: It's only about 5% of the gasket business today.

guidance.quote: we continue to continue to have a target group revenue target of about 18% to 20%
with margins being in the range of about 17-odd percent, a little bit maybe 17.5%
By year-end, everything should fall in line, which should be in the range of INR340 crores to INR350 crores.
We are targeting to take our exports to 35% by FY28.
we expect to grow about 17% this year, overall.

red_flags.label: Forging volume guidance cut and Marelli stake/court dispute
red_flags.quote: they're in the middle of court proceedings. So, by 30th September, we'll have a better picture.

red_flags.label: Forging productivity and manpower issues
red_flags.quote: There is a little you can say productivity came down. Every year it happens.

evasions.quote: Once the deal happens, we can't talk about today but that is the plan.
So, it's a mix of other income is a little less in this case in this quarter

summary.headline: Talbros posted a record Q1 FY27 with total income of INR242 crores (+15% YoY) and EBITDA of INR43 crores at a 17.6% margin, with management guiding FY27 group revenue growth of 18-20%.
summary.overview: Talbros reported record quarterly revenue of INR242 crores, up 15% YoY from INR211 crores, with EBITDA of INR43 crores (17.6% margin) and PAT of INR30 crores (+35% YoY). Gasket and heat shield revenue grew 21% to INR164 crores, while forging recovered only modestly to INR78 crores (+4%) amid weak European demand and manpower issues. Management said input-cost inflation (steel, aluminium, labour) temporarily compressed margins and expects to recover this from OEMs in coming quarters. New growth lines cited include data-centre generator gaskets (about 5% of gasket revenue) and a Stellantis chassis/forging programme that started production in Q1.

Margin under temporary pressure from commodity and labour costs
vs INR13 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores last year (as stated)

segments.name: Gasket & heat shield
segments.commentary: Revenue INR164 crores (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR29 crores (+32%). Claims nearly 50% share of domestic gasket market and is probably the largest heat shield (NVH) player in India; growth from Hyundai and Kia heat shields and data-centre gaskets.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78 crores (+4% YoY), EBITDA INR14 crores. Export-oriented (US, UK, Europe); Q1 hit by European demand softness, manpower shortages and lost Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.).

segments.name: Marelli Chassis Systems (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crores (+43% YoY), EBITDA INR17 crores, driven by passenger OEM volumes and value-added products. Management expects 30-40% growth for FY27 for this JV; Q1 margin dipped on lower other income and new manpower and rental costs.

segments.name: Talbros Marugo (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crores (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR6 crores (+57%), citing strong customer demand and efficiency gains.

segments.name: Lohum Talbros (JV)
segments.commentary: Circular-economy venture recovering carbon black and devulcanised rubber; described as progressing as planned, no financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided at 18-20%, with EBITDA margin around 17-17.5% as inflation impact is still being assessed.
Gasket division expected to grow about 17% in FY27, with FY27 gasket revenue of about INR680-700 crores.
Forging expected to grow 15-20% in FY27 to about INR340-350 crores, with Q2 at double-digit growth and Q4 the strongest quarter; July and August reported as improving on June.
Longer-term targets: gasket about INR850-900 crores and forging about INR600-700 crores by FY30; export share target 35% by FY28.
Sustainable EBITDA margin cited at around 17%. Capex planned at about INR103 crores for FY27 across gaskets, forgings and heat shields.
Management expects OEMs to pass through steel, aluminium and labour cost increases in coming quarters; Marelli margins expected to recover by year-end.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 capex of about INR103 crores across gaskets, forgings and heat shields, to meet OEM demand.
Forging equipment is in place; manpower and leadership issues reportedly resolved, with new CEO Ashish (appointed April 1) spending about 50% of time on forging.
Stellantis programme in the chassis division started production in Q1 FY27 after about 2 years of design changes and start of production.
Plastic EV components for JLR at about INR25 crores in orders, maturing from next financial year; JLR EV rubber components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. with supply from Q1/Q2 CY27.
Possible chassis plant in Gujarat under discussion with Tata Motors (management to meet Tata Motors chief within 90 days).
demand_pricing: Industry context: PV sales about 1.27 million units (+26% YoY), 2-wheelers 5.63 million units (+~20%), CV about 2.83 lakh units (+15%), EV PV volumes +87%, EV 2W about +68%.
Data centres: about 5% of gasket revenue today; estimated INR30-40 crores annual potential, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years; Cummins sales of INR25 crores in Q1 vs INR90 crores last year.
Management said 7 OEMs are looking to shift supply chains from China to India; BMW giving more business, Volvo a potential new gasket customer, and Stellantis opened for Marelli.
Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28 (wire harness, aftermarket and data-centre gaskets).
Forging orders: about INR500 crores over 5 years (about INR100 crores p.a.) cited; Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing in Q3-Q4.
Gasket pricing: management said data-centre gaskets are the same product as regular gaskets, with pricing unchanged; margins not separately disclosed.
Management stated pricing pass-through of input costs from OEMs is expected in coming quarters.
